- Well, is it him?
- Damned if I know... I'll check.
433:
- Excuse me, got a match?
- I don't smoke.
434:
- Well? - No, not him.
- A cop. - Right.
435:
The check showed the helmet isn't at any
of the addresses of Docent's accomplices.
436:
One last lead remains - Prokhorov,
the cloakroom attendant.
437:
However, we couldn't check it:
Prokhorov didn't show up for the meeting.
438:
Probably suspected something. Quit his job,
hasn't been home.
440:
For you - a thousand apologies, and many thanks.
Take off the wig, wash off the tattoos,
441:
go home, celebrate the New Year. Thank you very much.
- And my boys?
442:
We'll return your charges to their
place today.
443:
And if the cloakroom attendant turns up,
might we be needed again?
444:
I didn't want to tell you, but today
Bely - Docent - escaped from the colony.
445:
Unbelievable, but true. It's dangerous for you
to stay looking like this.
446:
Maybe tomorrow? It's New Year's after all, and
in their own way they tried too.
447:
We live out of town, it's unlikely
Docent could find us.
448:
All right, but don't take a step off the dacha!
Oh, and we forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev's wife, here's her reply.
Addressed to him.
450:
- You'll come to dinner on the first, promise?
- We promise!
451:
Pity, such good woman, and father -
fence, black-marketeer.
452:
What are you yelling about? Who let you go out?
- Look who's back... Bad person.
454:
The New Year has come. I wish that in this
new year everything will be new for you.
455:
Anything can happen, but know this:
wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I will always remember you,
I will definitely find you.
457:
- And now... Just a moment...
- Where's he off to?
458:
Who knows? You can't make anything
out with him these days.
459:
What's there to make out? Wherever you go, he says,
I'll find you and cut your throat.
461:
They say he took a razor to Ryaboy's throat - swish, and bye-bye.
- Gone totally savage, the jackal.
462:
Who's come to see you? Grandfather Frost
has come, and he's brought you presents!
463:
- Fedya, come here. - What did I do?
- Come on, come on. Wear them in good health. House slippers.
464:
- What the heck do I need them for? I don't even have a house.
- You will, it's all ahead of you.
465:
- And meanwhile they'll come in handy in prison. Wear them.
- All you do is croak doom.
466:
This is for you, Vasya... Gavrila Petrovich, this is for you.
- Thanks.
467:
- Pure wool.
- This is for you too.
469: Sour stuff. It's dull without vodka.
470:
- Do you have to get drunk as a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471:
We can just sit and have
a heart-to-heart.
472:
I'm no prosecutor to have heart-to-hearts with you.
- We could play a game.
473:
Get a load of him! Find yourself some sucker to play with!
You've got nine aces in your deck.
474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here's a good game - cities.
I say "Moscow",
476:
and you take the last letter, "A" - Astrakhan.
And you take "N" - Novgorod, understand?
477: And now you, Fedya, say one with "D".
478:
Vorkuta.
- Why? - I did time there.
479:
- All right. And you, then, with "A".
- Dzhambul. - What's Dzhambul got to do with it?
480:
Because it's warm there, my home is there,
my mama is there.
481:
Then let's play this way. I'll go out, you
hide something, I come back and find it.
482:
- You'd better find the helmet.
- Be quiet.
483:
- We hide, and he look through hole?
- Why? You go out and hide it.
484:
And you make sure I don't peek.
- Why me? Anything happens, it's Fedya.
485:
- I'll rip your jaw off, you little brat!
- Jaw, jaw...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- I was.
487:
- You had papa, mama?
- I did.
488: Why you so mean? Why like a dog?
490:
- Came on his own.
- Ah, you're here too.
491:
I tried your place, but I could feel
there was a stakeout.
492: Mityai, I need to lie low.
495:
- Sorry for troubling you for nothing, doctor.
- That's all right.
496:
Give him valerian, warm tea, and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read it.
499:
"Hello, dear papa! We found out
that you're in prison
500:
and were very glad, because we thought
you were dead."
501:
What scum snitched to that
little Khmyr about Khmyr?
502:
"And mama was glad too, because
when the letter came, she cried
503:
all day, and before she used to say
you were a test pilot."
505:
"But I'm still glad you're alive, because
mama says
506: you're a good man, just weak-willed."
507:
That's right! Weak-willed - swiped our common
money and pinned it on the cabbie.
508: Scram outta here! I'll knock your horns off, you radish!
510:
Shame on you! You're all 40 years old,
half your lives are already behind you.
511:
What's behind you? What's now?
What's ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, and nothing human!
Come to your senses before it's too late. That's my advice.
513:
Hey, Docent, we gotta clear out:
the doctor lady will snitch to the cops.
514:
- She won't. - Why?
- I did her in, razor across the throat...
515: she's lying in the well, go take a look.
516: How much I had? One year.
517: How much they give for escape? Three!
518:
How much for kindergarten and apartment?
Say ten!
520:
And for lousy 14 years I put up with
this snake?
521:
Who put old woman in well?
You do what you want, I go police.
523:
And you? You'll put up with him
until you die, is that it?
524:
Vas, the other day I tell him: I've got
a cold, and he...
525:
Enough, I'm sick of you and your cold.
Come here...
527:
- What are you doing?
- Gonna beat the carpet.
528:
Listen, comrades. Finita la commedia.
First of all, I'm taking this off.
530:
I'll serve my time and that's it. I'm going straight!
I'll get a job.
531:
- As what? - Watchman on my home collective farm.
- Why a watchman?
532:
I can shovel snow, lay bricks, or be
a translator - I know English.
533:
If only we bring hat too!
Docent who? Crook.
534:
- Many crooks, but only one hat.
- For the helmet they'd cut our sentence.
535: Where did he put it? We've checked everywhere.
536:
Crook! Did I tell you I had a cold?
And you: Jaw, jaw.
537:
- Made me dive in that freezing cold!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When they nabbed us. Remember, he says,
I'm fishing, and you dive.
539:
- Wait, what did he say then about fishing?
- I was fishing in an ice hole,
540:
- and then, Kosoy, he says, can you swim?
- He hid the helmet in the ice hole, that's what!
541:
That's it! You remembered, you bad person!
It's in the ice hole, in Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn't you say so? You lout! Could've at least left a note when you hanged yourself.
- Let's go.
543:
- And him?
- Never mind, let them pick him up. Lugging a hog like that. Let's go!
545:
- There's nothing there.
- It's there, on the bottom. Someone has to dive.
546:
Why me? Anything happens - it's Kosoy.
Vas, tell him to go in himself.
547: I can't! It's cold, I'll get sick.
548:
- A minute ago he was hanging himself, now he's scared of a cold!
- Sporting greetings!
550:
- Where's the boat station?
- Over there.
551: I'd waste you all, but there's no time to bother!
552:
Now there are two of them.
And one more at the dacha.
554:
- One!
- Well done, Fyodor Petrovich, well done!
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
